issues.title: [DEMO-1] CMDB lookup: fall back to mock when real ServiceNow returns no match
issues.body:
**As a** demo operator running with `AIOPS_USE_MOCK_ITSM=false`
**I want to** keep getting the mock CMDB's team + runbook mappings when the real ServiceNow PDI has no `cmdb_ci_service` row for a demo service
**So that** every verdict still routes to the right team with the right runbook, not the default `Platform On-Call` fallback

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14 in `/api/triage` response)
With `AIOPS_USE_MOCK_ITSM=false`, the registry routes `itsm.cmdb.lookup` to the real ServiceNow PDI. The PDI ships with no `payment`/`cart`/`checkout`/etc. CI records, so every lookup returns `ok=True, data=None`. Result:
- `assigned_team: "Platform On-Call"` (wrong — should be "Payments Team")
- `assigned_engineer: "oncall@platform-on-call.example.com"` (wrong)
- `recommended_runbook: null` (wrong)
- Decision trace: `"CMDB lookup returned no match; defaulted to Platform On-Call"`

## Root cause
`AIOPS_USE_MOCK_ITSM` is a single boolean that gates **three** capabilities together: `itsm.incident.create`, `itsm.incident.update`, **and** `itsm.cmdb.lookup`. In practice you want the real PDI for incident create/update (proves the integration) but the mock CMDB for the demo services. Today the flag forces both off.

## Task
Pick one of these (recommend option A):

**Option A — Real CMDB falls back to mock data on no-match (preferred).** In `aiops/tools/itsm/servicenow.py:cmdb_lookup`, when the ServiceNow query returns an empty result, look the service up in the mock table from `aiops/tools/mock_providers.py` and return that. Add a metadata flag `"fallback": "mock_cmdb"` so callers can see what happened.

**Option B — Split the env flag.** Replace `AIOPS_USE_MOCK_ITSM` with two flags:
- `AIOPS_ITSM_INCIDENT_PROVIDER=servicenow|mock` (default mock)
- `AIOPS_ITSM_CMDB_PROVIDER=mock|servicenow` (default mock)
Update `.env.example` + `mock_providers.py` + `servicenow.py` gates.

## Done when
- [ ] With `.env` configured for real ServiceNow incidents, a triage call on `payment` returns `assigned_team="Payments Team"`, `recommended_runbook` populated.
- [ ] Eval harness `--ci --min-pass-rate 0.85` stays green for `alert_triage`.
- [ ] Decision trace surfaces which CMDB path was used.

## Labels rationale
`itsm` (RA-003 surface), `demo-readiness` (surfaced by E2E test), `priority:high` (every demo verdict is wrong without it).

issues.title: [DEMO-2] LLM gateway: install configured SDK + real ping in /api/health
issues.body:
**As a** demo operator with `AIOPS_LLM_PROVIDER=openai` set
**I want to** see `/api/health` report whether the LLM is actually reachable
**So that** I notice when the SDK is missing or the API key is bad **before** RA-001 falls to its template summary and RA-002 collapses to Tier-4 keywords

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14)
- `/api/health` returns `"llm_provider": "openai"` (green chip in dashboard).
- Actual `/api/triage` response shows: RA-001 emits the **template fallback** summary (`"payment PaymentErrorRateHigh reported value 0.0500008... (source: Prometheus)."` — raw metric string, no narrative). RA-002 audit trace says `"LLM error: RuntimeError"` and `"Tier-4 keyword fallback chose application (keyword matches: 0)"`. Confidence `0.25`, root cause `"unable to determine from available signals"`.
- Net: the AI value of the POC is invisible to the demo audience.

## Root cause
Two issues stacked:

1. **SDK not installed.** `pyproject.toml` puts `openai>=1.40` in the `llm-openai` extra. `uv sync --extra dev --extra ui` doesn't include it. So `aiops/llm/openai_provider.py` raises `RuntimeError("openai SDK not installed")` on every call.
2. **Health endpoint never tries a real call.** It reads `os.environ.get("AIOPS_LLM_PROVIDER")` and returns it. SDK missing / bad key / wrong endpoint -> still green.

## Task
1. **Add an `llm_ok` field to `/api/health`** — issue a 1-token ping (cached for ~60 s to avoid hammering the API). Surface `llm_ok: bool`, `llm_provider`, `llm_model`, and `llm_error: str | null`. Dashboard chip stays green only when `llm_ok=true`.
2. **Document the LLM extra in `start.ps1` and `ONBOARDING.md`.** `start.ps1` should `uv sync` with the matching extra (`--extra llm-openai` when `AIOPS_LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, etc.), or fail loudly with a one-line instruction.
3. **Audit-trace visibility.** RA-001's `_generate_summary` and RA-002's classify already log to the trace. Make sure the dashboard surfaces "LLM unavailable — using template/Tier-4 fallback" prominently when it happens, not just in the trace text.

## Done when
- [ ] `/api/health` returns `llm_ok: false` with a useful `llm_error` when the SDK is missing or the API key is bad.
- [ ] `start.ps1` installs the right LLM extra automatically (or refuses to start with a clear message).
- [ ] On a working setup, RA-001 emits an LLM-generated summary (not the template fallback) and RA-002 reaches Tier 2 or 3 instead of Tier 4 for every demo scenario.

## Labels rationale
`demo-readiness` (silent fallback is the worst kind of bug for a POC), `priority:high` (without this the demo has no "AI").

issues.title: [DEMO-3] Auto-Ticketing: include description + classification + decision trace in ServiceNow incident
issues.body:
**As a** human triaging an incident in ServiceNow
**I want to** see the full triage context (summary, severity, classification, decision trace) in the incident's `description` field, not just a one-line `short_description`
**So that** the ticket is actually actionable without re-running the agent

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14)
ServiceNow incident `INC0010026` has `short_description="[Sev-1] payment: payment PaymentErrorRateHigh reported value 0.05000... (source: Prometheus)."` and **no description**. The incident shows up but a human opening it sees no narrative, no classification, no on-call info.

## Root cause
`agents/auto_ticketing/agent.py:ticket()` builds and passes `short_description` and `urgency` to `registry.call("itsm.incident.create", ...)`. The ServiceNow provider's `create_incident` already accepts a `description` parameter — the agent just doesn't pass one.

## Task
1. **Build a richer description body in `auto_ticketing/agent.py`.** Include:
    - The full `alert_summary` (RA-001's narrative, not template fallback if available)
    - Severity + confidence + assigned team + on-call engineer + runbook
    - The RA-001 decision trace (8 stages)
    - Empty placeholder for RA-002 classification — filled in by the route once #28 lands (see follow-up below)
2. **Pass `description=`, `assignment_group=` (= verdict.assigned_team), and `category=` (= incident_type when available) to the registry call.** All three are already supported by the ServiceNow provider.
3. **Follow-up coupling:** because RA-002 classifies *after* RA-003 tickets, the classification can't be in the create call today. Either reorder the pipeline (RA-002 before RA-003) OR call `itsm.incident.update` from the route after classification to append the classification block. **Recommend reorder** — classification doesn't depend on the ticket id.

## Done when
- [ ] A new ServiceNow incident has a `description` field with the multi-paragraph triage context.
- [ ] `assignment_group` matches the CMDB team (once DEMO-1 lands).
- [ ] `category` is set from the RA-002 incident_type when classification runs before ticketing.

## Out of scope
Screenshot/image attachment — tracked separately in DEMO-8.

## Labels rationale
`itsm`, `demo-readiness`, `priority:medium`.

issues.title: [DEMO-4] start.ps1 -Fresh: clear scenarios + state.db + chatops.jsonl on bring-up
issues.body:
**As a** demo operator running `start.ps1`
**I want to** start from a clean slate when I pass `-Fresh`
**So that** the dashboard doesn't show stale alerts, the verdicts table doesn't carry forward, and the chatops feed isn't polluted by yesterday's notifications

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14)
Three pieces of state survive a `stop.ps1` -> `start.ps1` cycle:

1. **flagd-config in the cluster.** Scenarios injected previously stay flipped on. Alert stream shows "1 payment failure" at startup even before any user interaction.
2. **`data/state.db`.** Verdicts, classifications, clusters all accumulate. `verdict_id=160` after a few hours of testing — most of which are from prior sessions.
3. **`demo/audit/chatops.jsonl`.** Yesterday's entries (timestamps from 2026-05-13T17:38...) still live alongside today's. `Get-Content -Wait` shows the full history.

## Task
1. **Add a `-Fresh` switch to `start.ps1`** (and equivalent `FRESH=1` env in `start.sh` if it exists). When set, before the cluster check:
    - `uv run python -m demo.failure_injection.inject --clear` — flips every scenario flag back to `off`.
    - `Remove-Item data/state.db -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` — fresh SQLite. `init_db()` re-creates it on the next FastAPI call.
    - Move `demo/audit/chatops.jsonl` to `demo/audit/chatops.jsonl.bak-<timestamp>` and start a new empty file (don't lose the history — just archive it).
2. **Document the flag** in `ONBOARDING.md` and the `start.ps1` header.
3. **Default `-Fresh` is OFF** — the existing behaviour (carry state forward) is the right default for iterative development.

## Done when
- [ ] `.\start.ps1 -Fresh` produces an empty alert stream, an empty verdicts list, and an empty chatops feed.
- [ ] `.\start.ps1` (no flag) keeps existing behaviour exactly as today.
- [ ] Archived `chatops.jsonl.bak-*` files are gitignored.

## Labels rationale
`demo-readiness`, `priority:medium`. Speeds up every iteration when rehearsing the demo.

issues.title: [DEMO-5] Dashboard: clarify Active scenarios vs Active alerts vs Prometheus rule shape
issues.body:
**As a** demo viewer watching the Overview page
**I want to** understand why "4 scenarios active -> 1 alert firing" is the right answer
**So that** I don't think the system is broken when the alert count lags the scenario count

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14)
Injected 4 scenarios: `payment_failure`, `payment_unreachable`, `product_catalog_failure`, `recommendation_cache_failure`. Dashboard shows "Active scenarios: 4" but "Active alerts: 1" (severity mix card and alert stream both show 1). Looks like 3 alerts are missing.

## Root cause (not a bug, but the UI doesn't say so)
Two unrelated effects stacked:

1. **Two scenarios share the same Prometheus rule.** `payment_failure` and `payment_unreachable` both fire `PaymentErrorRateHigh`. Prometheus emits **one** alert for a triggered rule, no matter how many flags caused it.
2. **Different `for:` windows.** `PaymentErrorRateHigh` fires in ~30 s. `ProductCatalogErrorRateHigh` and `RecommendationLatencyP95High` have longer `for:` windows (60-120 s). They will fire eventually, but the UI doesn't show "alerts pending".

## Task
1. **Show the scenario -> alert mapping on the Overview card.** Each scenario tile lists which Prometheus alert it triggers. When two scenarios share an alert, mark them with the same colour band.
2. **"Pending alerts" hint.** When a scenario is `Active` but its Prometheus alert hasn't fired yet, show a small "firing in ~Ns" countdown derived from the rule's `for:` window. Means we need the rule's `for:` value in the scenario YAML (or pulled from Prometheus rules API).
3. **Stat-card copy.** Rename "Active alerts" -> "Firing alerts" and add a tooltip: "Number of Prometheus rules currently in `firing` state. Each rule can be triggered by one or more injected scenarios."

## Done when
- [ ] Overview makes it obvious why injecting `payment_failure` + `payment_unreachable` produces one alert, not two.
- [ ] When a scenario is active but the rule hasn't crossed its window yet, the UI tells me "waiting ~60s for ProductCatalogErrorRateHigh to fire".

## Labels rationale

issues.title: [DEMO-7] Document Get-Content -Encoding UTF8 + cross-platform tail in ONBOARDING.md
issues.body:
**As a** dev on Windows tailing `demo/audit/chatops.jsonl`
**I want to** know that `Get-Content -Wait` mangles UTF-8 unless I add `-Encoding UTF8`
**So that** em-dashes don't show up as `â€”` and I don't waste 20 minutes thinking the file is corrupt

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14)
```
PS C:\Projects\AIops> Get-Content demo/audit/chatops.jsonl -Wait
{ ... "Routing reason: Sev-1 critical â€” page on-call regardless of hour" ... }
```
The file is valid UTF-8; PowerShell 5.1 reads it as the system code page (CP1252) and mangles every multi-byte character.

## Root cause
Windows PowerShell 5.1's `Get-Content` default encoding is `Default` (CP1252 on most US/EU machines), not UTF-8. PowerShell 7+ defaults to UTF-8, but `start.ps1` documents PS 5.1 as the supported shell.

## Task
Add a short "Tailing chatops audit log" section to `ONBOARDING.md`:
```powershell
# PowerShell 5.1 — explicit UTF-8
Get-Content demo/audit/chatops.jsonl -Wait -Encoding UTF8

# git-bash / WSL
tail -f demo/audit/chatops.jsonl
```
Link it from the existing "6 known gotchas" memory anchor and from the section in CLAUDE.md.

## Done when
- [ ] ONBOARDING.md has the command snippet under a clear heading.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's PowerShell tips section mentions the default-encoding gotcha if not already there.

## Labels rationale
`demo-readiness`, `priority:low`. 5-minute docs fix that saves the next person an hour.

issues.title: [DEMO-9] Fix verdict double-save in /api/triage handler
issues.body:
**As a** dev inspecting `data/state.db`
**I want to** see exactly one `verdicts` row per `/api/triage` call
**So that** `verdict_id` is a meaningful counter and the dashboard's verdict history isn't doubled

## Symptom (observed 2026-05-14)
After a few hours of testing, `verdict_id=160` in `/api/triage` responses. Roughly 80 actual triage calls were made — so every call is writing two rows.

## Root cause
Two writers:

1. `agents/alert_triage/agent.py:triage()` calls `state_repo.save_verdict(verdict, cluster_key=hit.cluster_key)` at the end of the 8-stage flow (and discards the returned id).
2. `demo/ui/server.py:triage_alert()` calls `state_repo.save_verdict(verdict, cluster_key=alert_obj.cluster_key())` again at the route handler, **just** to capture `verdict_id` so it can link the classification row to it.

Introduced when RA-002 (#48) wired in the classification table needing a foreign key to the verdict row.

## Task
Pick one (recommend option A):

**Option A — Have `triage()` return the saved id.** Change the signature of `triage(alert)` to return `(TriageVerdict, int)` where the int is the row id. Update `agents/alert_triage/__init__.py` exports + every call site (`demo/ui/server.py`, `agents/auto_ticketing/agent.py`, any tests). The route handler drops its `save_verdict` call.

**Option B — Move the save out of `triage()`.** The agent does the work, the route does the persistence. Cleaner separation but means `agents/auto_ticketing/agent.py` and the route both need to coordinate who saves what.

## Done when
- [ ] After 10 triage calls from a fresh `data/state.db`, `SELECT MAX(id) FROM verdicts` returns 10.
- [ ] `agents/alert_triage/evals/golden.json` still passes (no behaviour change to agent output).
- [ ] `verdict_id` in `/api/triage` response matches the actual row id.

## Labels rationale
`demo-readiness`, `priority:low`. Cosmetic; doesn't block anything but waste of disk + confusing during debugging.

issues.title: [DEMO-11] .env.example overhaul: Azure block, drop dead vars, document observability + UI vars
issues.body:
**As a** new contributor copying `.env.example` to `.env`
**I want to** see every env var the code actually reads, with sane defaults and comments
**So that** I don't get cryptic SDK errors at runtime or silently miss features I'm supposed to configure

## Symptom
Audit found six categories of drift between `.env`, `.env.example`, and the code that reads them. None individually breaks the demo, but together they make the env-var surface untrustworthy.

## Findings
1. **Azure block missing from `.env.example`.** Five keys live in `.env` (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`, `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME`, `AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION`) and the openai/anthropic providers read them, but `.env.example` documents none. A contributor switching LLM providers has to read source to know what to set.
2. **Dead vars in `.env.example`** that no code reads — delete or implement:
    - `AIOPS_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (line 4) — comment claims "applied by aiops/llm" but nothing reads it
    - `AIOPS_LLM_MAX_CALLS_PER_INCIDENT` (line 36) — claimed as a cost cap; only `AIOPS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_CALL` is actually applied in `aiops/llm/gateway.py`
    - `AIOPS_KIND_CLUSTER_NAME` (line 33) — leftover from kind/k3d era; project now uses Rancher Desktop k3s
    - `KUBECONFIG` (line 32) — empty in `.env`, never read
3. **Observability timeouts undocumented.** `aiops/tools/observability/prometheus.py:12` reads `AIOPS_PROMETHEUS_TIMEOUT`; `aiops/tools/observability/jaeger.py:16` reads `AIOPS_JAEGER_TIMEOUT`. Neither appears in `.env.example`.
4. **Jaeger URL / API prefix undocumented.** `demo/ui/server.py:657-658` reads `AIOPS_JAEGER_URL` and `AIOPS_JAEGER_API_PREFIX` for the topology endpoint. Demo operators bringing their own Jaeger will get 404s with no clue what to set.
5. **Alert broadcast interval undocumented.** `demo/ui/server.py:780` reads `AIOPS_ALERT_BROADCAST_INTERVAL` for the WebSocket push cadence.
6. **`AIOPS_SERVICENOW_TIMEOUT` / `AIOPS_SERVICENOW_RUNBOOK_FIELD` only in `.env.example`.** Code reads them (`aiops/tools/itsm/servicenow.py:66,244`) but `.env` doesn't carry them. Anyone copying `.env.example` -> `.env` loses these defaults silently if they prune comments.
7. **No `AIOPS_UI_PORT`.** `start.ps1:14` hardcodes `$UiPort = 8765`. Port conflicts force script edits.
8. **LLM provider/model defaults inconsistent.** `.env.example:2-3` says `anthropic` / `claude-sonnet-4-6`; `.env:2-3` says `openai` / `gpt-5`; `aiops/llm/base.py:75` defaults to `anthropic`. Three sources, three answers.

## Task
1. Add an explicit `# Azure OpenAI` block to `.env.example` (all five keys + comments).
2. Add an explicit `# Anthropic via Azure AI Foundry` block.
3. Delete the four dead vars (1.2 above).
4. Add `AIOPS_PROMETHEUS_TIMEOUT`, `AIOPS_JAEGER_TIMEOUT`, `AIOPS_JAEGER_URL`, `AIOPS_JAEGER_API_PREFIX`, `AIOPS_ALERT_BROADCAST_INTERVAL`, `AIOPS_UI_PORT` with their current code defaults.
5. Pick one canonical default for `AIOPS_LLM_PROVIDER` + `AIOPS_LLM_MODEL` and align `.env.example` and `aiops/llm/base.py` to match.
6. Read `start.ps1:14` to support `$env:AIOPS_UI_PORT` override.

## Done when
- [ ] Every env var that any code reads is documented in `.env.example`.
- [ ] No var in `.env.example` is unread by code.
- [ ] LLM provider default is consistent in three places.
- [ ] `start.ps1 -Port 9000` (or `$env:AIOPS_UI_PORT=9000; .\start.ps1`) works.

## Labels rationale
`demo-readiness`, `priority:medium`. Surfaced by audit 2026-05-14. Won't break the demo but every contributor wastes an hour learning the env-var surface from source.

issues.title: [DEMO-12] Consolidate demo/scenarios/ and demo/failure_injection/scenarios/ into one source of truth
issues.body:
**As a** contributor adding a new failure scenario
**I want to** drop a single YAML file in one obvious directory
**So that** the UI picks it up, the CLI picks it up, and the smoke test enforces a paired truth file — all automatically

## Symptom
Two scenario directories exist with overlapping purpose and different content:

| Directory | File count | Consumed by | Truth-file enforced by smoke test? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `demo/scenarios/` | 12 YAML | UI's `/api/scenarios` endpoint (via `_load_scenarios()` in `demo/ui/server.py`) | NO |
| `demo/failure_injection/scenarios/` | 3 YAML | CLI tool `demo.failure_injection.inject` | YES (`tests/test_smoke.py:114`) |

## Issues
1. **9 scenarios have no truth file, no enforcement.** The smoke test only walks `demo/failure_injection/scenarios/`. Truth-file discipline (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #8) silently lapses for 75% of demo scenarios.
2. **README confusion.** `demo/scenarios/README.md` and `demo/failure_injection/README.md` both describe scenario YAML schema. Neither explicitly says "don't use the other one". `demo/failure_injection/README.md:25` says "Drop a YAML file in `scenarios/`" without specifying which `scenarios/`.
3. **Drift risk.** Two directories will diverge — the CLI's set, the UI's set, and the truth-file set become three different things.

## Task
Pick one (recommend option A):

**Option A — One directory, both consumers.** Consolidate to `demo/scenarios/`:
- Move `demo/failure_injection/scenarios/*.yaml` into `demo/scenarios/` (keep filenames; no dup ids).
- Update `demo/failure_injection/inject.py` to read from `demo/scenarios/`.
- Update `tests/test_smoke.py:test_every_scenario_has_a_truth_file` to walk `demo/scenarios/`.
- Backfill truth files for the 9 UI-only scenarios (template in `demo/truth_files/template.yaml`).
- Delete `demo/failure_injection/scenarios/`.
- Merge the two READMEs into one at `demo/scenarios/README.md`; replace `demo/failure_injection/README.md` with a thin pointer.

**Option B — Two directories, two purposes, explicit naming.** Rename `demo/failure_injection/scenarios/` to `demo/failure_injection/cli_runnable/`, document that ALL scenario metadata lives in `demo/scenarios/` and the CLI dir is a subset of the cluster-applicable ones. Keep truth-file enforcement on `demo/scenarios/`.

## Done when
- [ ] There's one obvious place to add a new scenario YAML.
- [ ] The smoke test enforces a truth file for every scenario.
- [ ] `demo.failure_injection.inject --list` and `/api/scenarios` show the same set.
- [ ] Two READMEs no longer overlap in content.

## Labels rationale
`scenarios`, `demo-readiness`, `priority:medium`. Surfaced by audit 2026-05-14.

issues.title: [DEMO-15] Migrate @app.on_event("startup") to FastAPI lifespan context manager
issues.body:
**As a** maintainer
**I want to** stop seeing FastAPI deprecation warnings on every pytest run
**So that** the test log stays signal-only and the codebase is ready for a future FastAPI major

## Symptom
Three usages of `@app.on_event("startup")`, deprecated since FastAPI 0.104:
- `demo/ui/server.py:83` — `_bootstrap_state` (calls `init_db()`)
- `demo/ui/server.py:88` — `_register_chatops_adapters` (registers JsonFileChatOpsAdapter)
- `demo/ui/chatops_ws.py:122` — `_chatops_ws_bootstrap` (registers WebSocketChatOpsAdapter)

`pytest` logs show 8 DeprecationWarning entries from these.

## Task
Replace the three `@app.on_event` decorators with a single `lifespan` context manager passed to `FastAPI(lifespan=...)`. Pattern:
```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    get_chatops_client().register(JsonFileChatOpsAdapter(...))
    _register_chatops_ws_adapter(app)
    yield
    # teardown — none today

app = FastAPI(title=..., lifespan=lifespan)
```

The chatops_ws.py case needs a small refactor — currently it registers via `@app.on_event` inside a function `register_routes(app)`. Either expose a separate `bootstrap_adapter(app)` function called from the lifespan, or merge the adapter registration into the parent lifespan.

## Done when
- [ ] No `@app.on_event` remains in the codebase.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -W default` shows no FastAPI DeprecationWarning entries.
- [ ] All existing tests still pass.

## Labels rationale
`demo-readiness`, `priority:low`. Pure cleanup; PR #47 flagged it during review.
